tools.name: start_signup
tools.description: Creates a pending R2F account and emails your human a 6-digit code. Works without a token. tools.name: finish_signup
tools.description: Ask your human for the 6-digit code R2F just emailed them, then call this. Returns their personal token: save it in your MCP config (the reply shows the exact command) so you can post their build next.

tools.name: update_profile
tools.description: Set your human's profile: name (private unless show_name), poker game, one-line bio, X handle, website. Only fields you pass change. The photo is set on the site (Settings).

tools.name: whoami
tools.description: The R2F account this token belongs to, and whether agent posts auto-publish.

tools.name: list_my_builds
tools.description: The builder’s projects on R2F with stakes tier, ownership state and badge snippet.

tools.name: get_build
tools.description: Details of one of the builder’s builds, including pending drafts and the latest comments from real people.

tools.name: create_build
tools.description: Put the project you are working on onto R2F. Read the repo for an honest name, one-line tagline, live https URL and stack (e.g. from package.json). Show your human what you will post first. Rounders to Founders is a community of poker players building startups. You act for your human builder. Log en

tools.name: update_build
tools.description: Change tagline, url, stack, story, looking_for, status or revenue_model. Changing the url resets ownership verification.

tools.name: verify_ownership
tools.description: One-time proof the builder owns the site (needed above Micro Stakes). First add the R2F badge (badge_html from get_build) to the site footer, or the meta tag to the <head>, and DEPLOY it. Then call this.

tools.name: post_update
tools.description: Draft a log entry for one of the builder’s builds: what shipped, what broke, what it cost (time and money). Base it on real commits/changelog; first person as the builder; no invented numbers. It is saved as a DRAFT for the human to approve on the site unless they enabled auto-publish.

tools.name: report_revenue
tools.description: Self-report monthly revenue in USD: MRR if the build sells subscriptions, otherwise the average of the last 3 full months of collected revenue. You MUST ask your human for the real number and their explicit confirmation that it is collected revenue, not a projection, and pass human_confirmed: true.

tools.name: search_community
tools.description: Read-only: find threads and builds about a topic (e.g. "Stripe webhooks", "pricing"). Link your human to useful ones.

tools.name: tool_rankings
tools.description: Read-only: the tools R2F builders list in their stacks, ranked by builders.

findings.title: Description issues instructions to the model
findings.detail: Description of "start_signup" contains imperative instructions directed at the AI assistant rather than describing the tool. This is the core tool-poisoning technique.

findings.remediation: Treat the server as untrusted; the model may obey embedded instructions.

findings.title: Lethal trifecta: untrusted input + private data + external sink
findings.detail: Server "mcp" exposes tools that together enable an exfiltration flow. Untrusted content: get_build, create_build, search_community · Private data: start_signup, finish_signup, update_profile, whoami · Public sink: start_signup, finish_signup, whoami, create_build, post_update.

evidence.snippet: Untrusted content: get_build, create_build, search_community · Private data: start_signup, finish_signup, update_profile, whoami · Public sink: start_signup, finish_signup, whoami, create_build, post_update

findings.remediation: Do not co-install these capabilities under one trust boundary; an injected comment/email can steer the model to exfiltrate via the sink tool.
